title: Sparse hole punching through Namespace and daemon APIs
scope: Namespace::punch_hole and Namespace::handle_punch_hole, resident fs-punch-hole/fs-hpunch-hole RPC, and offline fs-punch-hole CLI
Inline range zeroing without promotion; the inline allocated_size remains unchanged
Chunked partial-edge zeroing and fully covered chunk removal, with a 1 TiB sparse-range regression that does not iterate over hole chunks
File size and bytes outside the interval remain unchanged; zero-length and offset-at-or-beyond-EOF calls do not publish or update timestamps after normal access and inode append-only checks
C++ path behavior on both storage backends: symlink following, hard-link identity, snapshots/forks and reopen; modern backend additionally covers GC

Modern backend handle behavior: duplicate shared cursor, unlink with path reuse, read-only EBADF, inode append-only EPERM, immutable path refusal with admitted writable-handle success, and descriptor O_APPEND not imposing inode append-only policy

Resident RPC validation: malformed signed-range arguments leave sequence, data, metadata and cursor unchanged; foreign/closed handle ownership returns EBADF+1; another session mount lease returns EBUSY+1
Offline CLI range operation and repository consistency check

baseline_probe.status: passed; unsupported APIs rejected without state change
baseline_probe.qualification: The new C++ Namespace methods do not exist on the baseline, so no C++ baseline test was attempted. The baseline differential probes RPC path/handle operations and offline CLI only.

explicit_exclusions: No FSKit production callback or native mounted F_PUNCHHOLE syscall behavior is implemented or claimed.
No Preallocate protocol, F_PREALLOCATE, posix_fallocate, reservation guarantee, or physical extent query is implemented or claimed.
Inline representation remains allocated after punching; this operation does not promise inline deallocation or allocated_size reduction.
Raw Journal orphan range-erasure fallback was reviewed statically but was not independently forced by a dedicated test; no distinct test claim is made for it.
This is C++/daemon RPC/offline CLI validation, not native filesystem compatibility evidence.
